name: Amikacin
route_note: IV or IM with therapeutic drug monitoring; once-daily liposomal inhalation (Arikayce) for MAC lung disease.
targets: 16S rRNA of the 30S ribosomal subunit (A site)

discovery.note: Made by acylating kanamycin A with an L-hydroxyaminobutyric acid side chain, which blocks many aminoglycoside-modifying enzymes.

tagline: Enzyme-resistant aminoglycoside for resistant Gram-negatives and mycobacteria
summary: Amikacin is a semi-synthetic aminoglycoside derived from kanamycin A. Its side chain protects it from most aminoglycoside-modifying enzymes, so it often remains active against gentamicin- and tobramycin-resistant Gram-negative bacteria and is used against nontuberculous mycobacteria.
mechanism: Aminoglycosides are polycationic molecules that cross the Gram-negative outer membrane by self-promoted uptake and enter the cytoplasm by an oxygen-dependent transport process, which is why they are inactive against anaerobes. Inside, they bind the decoding A site of 16S rRNA in the 30S subunit, causing misreading of mRNA and production of aberrant proteins that damage the membrane, accelerating uptake; killing is rapid and concentration-dependent.

The L-HABA side chain at the 1-amino position sterically hinders most acetylating, phosphorylating and adenylating enzymes, preserving activity; it remains vulnerable to AAC(6')-I enzymes and to 16S rRNA methyltransferases such as ArmA and RmtB.
uses: Serious infections caused by aminoglycoside-resistant Gram-negative bacilli
Nontuberculous mycobacterial infections (Mycobacterium avium complex, M. abscessus)

history.title: Kanamycin
history.detail: Hamao Umezawa isolates kanamycin from Streptomyces kanamyceticus in Japan.

history.title: Clinical use
history.detail: Amikacin (Amikin) enters clinical use in the mid-1970s.

history.title: Liposomal inhalation
history.detail: The FDA grants accelerated approval to Arikayce for refractory MAC lung disease, with a boxed warning for respiratory adverse reactions.

history.title: EU approval
history.detail: The European Commission authorises Arikayce liposomal.

history.title: WHO TB guidance
history.detail: WHO's six-month BPaLM regimen for drug-resistant TB reduces reliance on injectable agents such as amikacin.

pk.bioavailability: negligible orally; inhaled liposomes give high lung concentrations with low systemic exposure

safety.boxed_warning: Parenteral labels warn of ototoxicity, nephrotoxicity and neuromuscular blockade; Arikayce carries a boxed warning for increased respiratory adverse reactions (hypersensitivity pneumonitis, haemoptysis, bronchospasm, exacerbation).

facts: Hearing loss is the dominant dose-limiting toxicity of amikacin in long TB and NTM courses.
